description: This topic explores how chemical industries convert raw materials into useful products, the factors governing where they are sited, key manufacturing processes such as the Haber and Contact processes, and the economic and environmental impact of chemical industries in Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Which raw materials are combined in the Haber process to manufacture ammonia?
mcq.explanation: Ammonia (NH3) is made in the Haber process by combining nitrogen and hydrogen: N2 + 3H2 reversibly forms 2NH3.

mcq.questionText: In the Contact process, sulphur dioxide is converted to sulphur trioxide over which catalyst?
mcq.explanation: The conversion 2SO2 + O2 reversibly forms 2SO3 uses vanadium(V) oxide (V2O5) as the catalyst in the Contact process.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT normally a factor considered when siting a chemical industry?

options.text: The colour of the factory building

mcq.explanation: Factors such as raw materials, water, energy, transport, labour, market and waste disposal matter; the colour of the building has no economic or technical importance.

mcq.questionText: Which catalyst is used in the Haber process?
mcq.explanation: The Haber process uses finely divided iron as the catalyst to speed up the formation of ammonia.

mcq.questionText: The main use of ammonia produced by the Haber process is in the manufacture of:
mcq.explanation: Most ammonia is used to make nitrogenous fertilisers such as ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate and urea.

mcq.questionText: In the Contact process, the absorption of sulphur trioxide is carried out using:

options.text: Concentrated sulphuric acid to form oleum

mcq.explanation: SO3 is absorbed in concentrated sulphuric acid to form oleum (H2S2O7), which is then diluted with water to give sulphuric acid. Direct addition to water produces a dangerous mist.

mcq.questionText: The Solvay process is used industrially to manufacture:
mcq.explanation: The Solvay (ammonia-soda) process manufactures sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) from brine, ammonia and carbon dioxide.

mcq.questionText: Which raw materials are the main starting materials in the Solvay process?
mcq.explanation: The Solvay process uses brine (concentrated NaCl solution) and limestone (CaCO3, which supplies CO2 and ammonia is recycled) to produce sodium carbonate.

mcq.questionText: Soap is manufactured by boiling fats or oils with:
mcq.explanation: Soap is made by saponification: boiling fats or oils with hot concentrated sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) produces soap and glycerol.

mcq.questionText: Why is a chemical industry that uses bulky, heavy raw materials usually located near the source of those materials?

options.text: To reduce the cost of transporting the raw materials
To increase the selling price of products
To make the products more colourful

mcq.explanation: Transporting heavy or bulky raw materials over long distances is costly, so industries such as cement works are sited near limestone deposits to cut transport costs.

mcq.questionText: Which gas is the main air pollutant released when sulphide ores are roasted or fossil fuels are burned, and which causes acid rain?
mcq.explanation: Sulphur dioxide (SO2) escaping from chemical plants dissolves in rainwater to form acidic solutions, causing acid rain that damages plants, buildings and aquatic life.

mcq.questionText: An example of an East African chemical industry that manufactures cement is found at:
mcq.explanation: The Wazo Hill cement factory (Twiga/Tanzania Portland Cement) near Dar es Salaam is a well-known Tanzanian chemical industry that uses local limestone.

mcq.questionText: Which statement best describes a by-product of a chemical industry?

options.text: The main substance the factory is built to produce
A secondary substance formed alongside the main product
The raw material fed into the process
The energy used to drive the reaction

mcq.explanation: A by-product is a secondary substance produced together with the main product; for example glycerol is a by-product of soap manufacture and can itself be sold.

mcq.questionText: Why is a moderate pressure of about 200 atmospheres and a temperature of about 450 degrees Celsius chosen for the Haber process rather than very high pressure and very low temperature?

options.text: Because these conditions give a reasonable yield of ammonia at an acceptable rate and cost
Because ammonia cannot form at any other conditions
Because the catalyst only works above 1000 degrees Celsius
Because nitrogen boils at exactly 450 degrees Celsius

mcq.explanation: Very high pressure is expensive and dangerous; a very low temperature gives a high equilibrium yield but is far too slow. About 200 atm and 450 degrees Celsius with an iron catalyst is a practical compromise between yield, rate and cost.

mcq.questionText: Quality control in a chemical industry is mainly concerned with:

options.text: Ensuring products meet a required standard of purity and composition
Increasing the number of workers only

mcq.explanation: Quality control involves testing raw materials and finished products to make sure they have the correct purity, concentration and properties before sale.

fib.questionText: The industrial manufacture of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen is called the _____ process.
fib.explanation: The Haber process combines nitrogen and hydrogen over an iron catalyst to make ammonia.

fib.questionText: The manufacture of sulphuric acid on a large scale is carried out by the _____ process.
fib.explanation: The Contact process produces sulphuric acid through the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide.

fib.questionText: In the Contact process, sulphur dioxide is oxidised to sulphur trioxide using the catalyst _____.
fib.explanation: Vanadium(V) oxide (V2O5) catalyses the reaction 2SO2 + O2 reversibly forms 2SO3.

fib.questionText: The reaction between nitrogen and hydrogen in the Haber process is _____, meaning it can proceed in both directions.
fib.explanation: The Haber reaction is reversible (an equilibrium), so unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen are recycled to improve overall yield.

fib.questionText: The raw materials brine and limestone are used in the _____ process to manufacture sodium carbonate.
fib.explanation: The Solvay (ammonia-soda) process makes sodium carbonate from brine, limestone and ammonia.

fib.questionText: The conversion of fats or oils to soap by boiling with sodium hydroxide is called _____.
fib.explanation: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats or oils to form soap and glycerol.

fib.questionText: When soap is made, the useful by-product formed alongside the soap is _____.
fib.explanation: Saponification of fats produces soap and glycerol (glycerine), which can be sold for use in cosmetics and medicines.

fib.questionText: Sulphur dioxide escaping from a chemical plant dissolves in rainwater and causes _____ rain, which damages buildings and crops.
fib.explanation: SO2 forms acidic solutions in rainwater, producing acid rain that corrodes structures and harms living things.

fib.questionText: In the Haber process the unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen are _____ back into the reactor to avoid wasting raw materials.
fib.explanation: Because the reaction is reversible and incomplete, leftover gases are recycled to improve the overall conversion to ammonia.

fib.questionText: The Tanzanian cement industry at Wazo Hill near Dar es Salaam mainly uses the local raw material _____.
fib.explanation: Cement manufacture uses limestone (calcium carbonate), so cement factories are sited near limestone deposits to reduce transport costs.

tf.questionText: The Haber process uses an iron catalyst to speed up the formation of ammonia.
tf.explanation: Finely divided iron is the catalyst used in the Haber process.

tf.questionText: In the Contact process, sulphur trioxide is added directly to water to make sulphuric acid in industry.
tf.explanation: Adding SO3 directly to water produces a dangerous acid mist, so SO3 is first absorbed in concentrated sulphuric acid to form oleum, which is then diluted.

tf.questionText: Most of the ammonia made by the Haber process is used to manufacture nitrogenous fertilisers.
tf.explanation: Ammonia is mainly converted into fertilisers such as ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate and urea.

tf.questionText: The availability of water is not important when deciding where to site a chemical industry.
tf.explanation: Water is essential for cooling, dissolving substances and as a reactant, so a reliable water supply is an important siting factor.

tf.questionText: A chemical industry contributes to a country's economy by creating jobs and earning foreign exchange.
tf.explanation: Chemical industries provide employment, supply useful products, and can earn foreign currency through exports, boosting the economy.

tf.questionText: The reaction between nitrogen and hydrogen in the Haber process goes to completion in one pass.
tf.explanation: The reaction is reversible and only partially converts the gases in one pass, so unreacted gases are recycled.

tf.questionText: Vanadium(V) oxide is the catalyst used in the Contact process.
tf.explanation: V2O5 catalyses the oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide in the Contact process.

tf.questionText: Proper treatment of factory waste before release into rivers helps to reduce water pollution.
tf.explanation: Treating effluent removes or neutralises harmful substances, protecting aquatic life and people who use the water.

tf.questionText: Sodium carbonate produced by the Solvay process is used in glass making and as a water softener.
tf.explanation: Sodium carbonate (soda ash) is widely used in the manufacture of glass, soaps and detergents and to soften hard water.

tf.questionText: Quality control is unnecessary in a chemical industry because all products are automatically pure.
tf.explanation: Products are not automatically pure; quality control tests are essential to ensure they meet the required standards of purity and composition.

summary.questionText: State four factors that should be considered when deciding where to site a chemical industry.
summary.correctAnswer: Availability of raw materials, supply of energy and water, good transport links, and availability of labour (other valid factors include nearness to the market and a means of safe waste disposal).
summary.explanation: Siting decisions balance the cost and availability of inputs (raw materials, energy, water, labour) with access to markets, transport and waste disposal to keep production economical.

summary.questionText: Write the balanced equation for the formation of ammonia in the Haber process and state the conditions used.
summary.correctAnswer: N2 + 3H2 reversibly forms 2NH3; conditions: about 200 atmospheres pressure, about 450 degrees Celsius and a finely divided iron catalyst.
summary.explanation: These conditions give a practical compromise between a reasonable equilibrium yield of ammonia and a fast enough reaction rate at acceptable cost.

summary.questionText: Outline the three main stages of the Contact process for making sulphuric acid.
summary.correctAnswer: Stage 1: burn sulphur (or roast sulphide ore) in air to make sulphur dioxide, S + O2 forms SO2. Stage 2: oxidise sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide over vanadium(V) oxide, 2SO2 + O2 reversibly forms 2SO3. Stage 3: absorb SO3 in concentrated sulphuric acid to form oleum, then dilute with water to give sulphuric acid.
summary.explanation: The Contact process makes SO2, catalytically converts it to SO3, then converts SO3 to H2SO4 via oleum to avoid producing a hazardous acid mist.

summary.questionText: Explain why the chemical industry is important to a country's economy.
summary.correctAnswer: It creates employment, supplies useful products such as fertilisers, acids and cement, adds value to local raw materials, earns foreign exchange through exports and reduces dependence on imports.
summary.explanation: Chemical industries turn raw materials into valuable goods, support agriculture and other industries, and contribute to national income and development.

summary.questionText: Describe two ways in which a chemical industry can cause pollution and one method of controlling it.
summary.correctAnswer: Pollution: release of harmful gases such as sulphur dioxide into the air, and discharge of toxic liquid effluent into rivers. Control: treat or neutralise waste before release, install scrubbers or filters to trap gases, and recycle by-products instead of dumping them.
summary.explanation: Air and water pollution from gases and effluent can be reduced by treating waste, using scrubbers, and recycling by-products to protect the environment.

summary.questionText: Give the meaning of the terms raw material, product and by-product in a chemical industry.
summary.correctAnswer: A raw material is the starting substance fed into the process; a product is the main useful substance the factory is built to make; a by-product is a secondary substance formed alongside the main product, which may also be useful.
summary.explanation: For example, in soap making the fats and sodium hydroxide are raw materials, soap is the product and glycerol is a by-product.

summary.questionText: State three large-scale uses of sulphuric acid.
summary.correctAnswer: Manufacture of fertilisers (such as ammonium sulphate and superphosphate), making detergents and paints, refining petroleum, and as the electrolyte in lead-acid car batteries (any three).
summary.explanation: Sulphuric acid is one of the most widely used industrial chemicals, especially in fertiliser production and battery manufacture.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between the laboratory preparation and large-scale industrial manufacture of a chemical.
summary.correctAnswer: Laboratory preparation makes small quantities for study or testing, uses simple glassware and is not usually concerned with cost or recycling. Industrial manufacture makes large quantities continuously, uses large specialised plant, recycles unreacted materials and aims to maximise yield while minimising cost and waste.
summary.explanation: Scale, equipment, continuity, cost considerations and recycling are the main differences between laboratory and industrial production.

summary.questionText: Briefly describe how sodium carbonate is made by the Solvay process.
summary.correctAnswer: Carbon dioxide and ammonia are passed into concentrated brine, forming sodium hydrogencarbonate which precipitates out; this is heated to give sodium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide. The ammonia and carbon dioxide are recovered and recycled.
summary.explanation: The Solvay process converts brine and limestone into sodium carbonate while recycling ammonia and carbon dioxide to reduce costs.

summary.questionText: Give two examples of chemical industries found in Tanzania or East Africa and state a raw material each uses.
summary.correctAnswer: Cement industry (for example Wazo Hill, Dar es Salaam) uses limestone; fertiliser industry uses materials such as natural gas or phosphate rock. Other examples include soap and edible oil industries that use vegetable oils.
summary.explanation: Tanzanian chemical industries are usually sited near their raw materials, such as cement works near limestone deposits.

hoq.questionText: The Haber reaction N2 + 3H2 reversibly forms 2NH3 is exothermic. A student suggests using a very low temperature to increase the yield of ammonia. What is the main practical problem with this suggestion?

options.text: A very low temperature makes the reaction far too slow even with a catalyst
A very low temperature would decompose the ammonia completely
The iron catalyst would melt at low temperature
Nitrogen cannot exist as a gas at low temperature

hoq.explanation: Lowering the temperature does favour a higher equilibrium yield of ammonia (the forward reaction is exothermic), but it also slows the rate so much that ammonia would be produced too slowly to be economical. About 450 degrees Celsius is a compromise between yield and rate.

hoq.questionText: A new chemical factory will roast large amounts of sulphide ore and needs huge quantities of water for cooling. Which site would be the most suitable and economical?

options.text: Near the ore deposit and close to a reliable river, with arrangements to treat gases and effluent
In the middle of a city far from any water source
On a remote mountain top with no roads
In a national park to keep it hidden from people

hoq.explanation: Roasting bulky ore means the plant should be near the ore to cut transport costs, and it needs a reliable water supply for cooling. It must also have transport links and treat its sulphur dioxide gas and effluent to control pollution.

hoq.questionText: In a soap factory, fats are boiled with concentrated sodium hydroxide. Common salt is then added to the mixture. Why is the salt added?

options.text: To make the soap separate out (salt out) from the solution so it can be collected
To act as the catalyst for saponification
To convert the fat into sodium hydroxide

hoq.explanation: Adding common salt to the mixture reduces the solubility of soap, causing it to separate (salt out) as a solid layer at the top, leaving glycerol and excess alkali in the solution below.
